claims.text: Equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi can exist in a simple solid-solution state.
The combination of deformation behavior, hardness, and strength in this alloy is governed by lattice distortion.
The relevant lattice distortion hinders dislocation movement.
Hindrance of dislocation movement produces a trade-off between plasticity and strength.
Changing the CoCrFeNiTi composition can introduce or modify lattice distortions.
Differences in atomic radii among Co, Cr, Fe, Ni, and Ti cause lattice distortion.
Differences in bonding characteristics among Co, Cr, Fe, Ni, and Ti cause lattice distortion.
Lattice distortions act as obstacles to dislocation movement and thereby influence strength and plasticity.
An optimized degree or type of lattice distortion will improve strength relative to the starting alloy while maintaining favorable plasticity.
The hypothesis is limited to compositions within ±5% of an equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi composition.
The hypothesis applies from 25 °C to 600 °C under uniaxial compression or tension.
Failure of composition-induced lattice-distortion changes to produce the predicted changes in strength and plasticity would falsify the hypothesis.
